title: Somewhere in My Heart
year_note: On Love, released 9 November 1987. The single followed on 11 April 1988.

notes.made: Roddy Frame made Love between April and August 1987 with American producers, after time in New York listening to WBLS. This one was made with the Jonzun Crew in Boston: Michael Jonzun produced it, played drums, programmed keyboards and sang backing vocals. Frame said he wanted to make 'a Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis kinda record', marrying New York R&B electro to his own British songwriting.
notes.context: Frame called the album his Young Americans. He thought this song was the runt of the litter and almost left it off, saying it would be best as a B-side. Love entered at 49 and only climbed to 10 after this single went to 3 in the UK in spring 1988; by then he was living in a wooden shack in Marple Bridge.

listen_for.note: Michael Jonzun's drums and programmed keyboards, made with his Jonzun Crew in Boston, under a Scottish songwriter's guitar pop.

listen_for.where: the backing vocals in the chorus
listen_for.note: Jonzun again. The whole production is one Boston producer around Frame's voice.

leads_to.title: What Have You Done for Me Lately
leads_to.why: The Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis sound Frame was aiming at, recorded at Flyte Tyme in Minneapolis in September 1985.

notes.unverified: Desmond's 'Roddy Frame's biggest hit, UK #3' matches the chart; I didn't check every other Aztec Camera single to confirm 'biggest'.

culture.title: The runt goes top 3
culture.line: Released on 11 April 1988, the song Roddy Frame nearly left off Love reached 3 in the UK and pulled the album up from 49 to 10.

culture.title: Radar Films video
culture.line: John Scarlett-Davis directed the video, produced by Nick Verden for Radar Films.
